title: What is known about 1RB1RE_0LC0LF_0LA0LD_1LE1LC_1RA0LB_---0RE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RE_0LC0LF_0LA0LD_1LE1LC_1RA0LB_---0RE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The machine rewrites the left end of a word of blocks an and xn: each sweep of the head turns one x into three a (proved in Lean for all block lengths, with or without a stack of a's to the left). The rules for the deeper levels of the word are only observed, so no map is known yet. No halt in 109 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 33,485 cells have been visited and 18,463 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.37). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.058).

claims.title: The basic sweeps
claims.text: 0^inf E> 0 a^(p+1) 0 x^(q+1) → 0^inf E> 0 a^(p+4) 0 x^q in 4p + 26 steps, and against a stack of a's, L a 1 E> 0 a^k 0 x^(q+1) → L 1 E> 0 a^(k+3) 0 x^q in 4k + 24 steps, for all values and any tapes L, R.

claims.title: The next level, observed
claims.text: With first blocks a^p 0 a^m 0 x^q and m ≤ q, the left end goes (p, m, q) → (1, 3m + p + 1, q − m), e.g. (1, 11, 4023) → (1, 35, 4012) → (1, 107, 3977) → ... and (714, 1491, 6138) → (1, 5188, 4647). For m > q the next level of the word is rewritten and the counter y^K at the right end sometimes gains one. Seen in simulation, not proved.

claims.title: Where it would halt
claims.text: The only halting transition is F reading 0; F is entered only from B reading 1, which follows E reading 1. So the machine halts exactly when the head in state E reads a 1 with 0 1 to its left (from the transition table).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The basic sweeps are proved, but the rules for the deeper levels of the word, and so a map on the block lengths, are not found yet (see "For later" in the README).

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_0LD0LF_0LB0LE_1LA1LD_---0RA up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

check: gcc -O2 -o events holdouts/1RB1RE_0LC0LF_0LA0LD_1LE1LC_1RA0LB_---0RE/c/events.c && ./events 1RB1RE_0LC0LF_0LA0LD_1LE1LC_1RA0LB_---0RE 1000000000 L 1 a=10 x=1000 | grep "E> 0 a"

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine works on the left end of a word made of blocks of two kinds, a = 10 and x = 1000: each trip of the head turns one x into three a. That much is proved; how the deeper blocks get rewritten is still being decoded.

facts.text: The basic sweep, proved in Lean for all block lengths.
No halt in the C simulator.
Rules of the deeper levels not yet found.

sections.eyebrow: What the tape is made of
sections.heading: Blocks of a and x
html: With a = 10 and x = 1000, whenever the head is at the left end in state E the tape reads
E>0 a^p 0 x^q a^r 0 x^s ... y^K a^3 0
a list of blocks and, at the right end, a counter of K copies of y = a40 that gains one now and then (K = 46 at step 4.3·108, 51 at 9·108), so the right side grows like the logarithm of time.

Each sweep of the head over the first two blocks turns one x into three a: (p, q) → (p + 3, q − 1). When the x's run out, the next block of a's is moved onto a stack at the left and the same sweep repeats, each one taking an a from the stack: with first blocks a^p 0 a^m 0 x^q and m ≤ q the result is (1, 3m + p + 1, q − m). For example (1, 11, 4023) → (1, 35, 4012) → (1, 107, 3977) → (1, 323, 3870) → (1, 971, 3547) → (1, 2915, 2576).

sections.heading: Open
html: The machine halts exactly when the head in state E reads a 1 with 0 1 to its left. The basic sweeps never do that. When m > q the deeper blocks are rewritten in ways that have been seen but not yet written down as rules; those rules, iterated, would turn the question into one about a map on the block lengths, which looks Collatz-like (one regime multiplies a count by 3/2).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.37). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.058).
After 109 steps the tape spans 33,485 cells (27,314 left of the start, 96 right), with a density of 1s of 0.551.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: A rewriting system on the left end of a word of blocks a^n, x^n (a = 10, x = 1000) with a slow counter y^K at the right; each sweep turns one x into three a. Basic rules proved in Lean; the nested map not yet found.
